section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the desire for mitzvos is an essential desire, and that through teshuvah one reaches the essential delight of Atzmus Ein Sof, which also draws down the desire for mitzvos, and this illuminates why tefillin are called "mochin" and how even one act of laying tefillin draws this essential delight.
section.t: And this can be understood in more detail based on what is explained in the discourses of the Rebbe
(the Rebbe Rashab)
of blessed memory,
that the desire for mitzvos is an essential desire in which change does not apply,
and also that which through teshuvah the blemishes that one blemished in Torah and mitzvos are filled,
this is not in the category of regret or change, G-d forbid,
but rather,
that through teshuvah one reaches the essential delight of the innerness and Atzmus of Ein Sof,
which is the delight in Yisrael from their own essence
(in addition to the delight that comes from their fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos),
and when the essential delight is drawn down,
the desire is also drawn down.
And based on this, it will be better understood why tefillin are called "mochin" (intellect),
for that Yisrael are one nation in the land
(as stated in the tefillin of the Master of the world),
that even when they are in the land they are attached and bound with Hashem Echad,
is because the root of Yisrael is in the essential delight of the innerness and Atzmus of Ein Sof
(therefore matters of the land cannot cause a change in this),
and through the fulfillment of the mitzvah of tefillin,
this matter is drawn down in revelation.
And this is also that which "a skull that does not lay tefillin"
has a special law
is specifically when he has never laid them,
and through laying tefillin one time,
he leaves this category,
for through laying tefillin
(even through one time)
the revelation of the essential delight is drawn into him.
And it can be said,
that through this the desire for Torah and mitzvos is also drawn down,
in the manner of what was explained above regarding the matter of teshuvah.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the root of Yisrael is in the level of "not a man" where change does not apply, and through serving with Netzach (eternity), one draws down the treasures from above in a manner of endless eternity and lavish giving, leading to the ultimate victory of Hashem's kingship.
section.t: And this is "And also the Eternal One of Yisrael does not lie and does not relent, for He is not a man to relent,"
that the root of Yisrael is in the level of "not a man,"
above even a hidden rationale,
in which change does not apply, G-d forbid.
[And together with this,
there is in this also the advantage of "man,"
the matter of "rationale,"
the essential delight].
And through a person performing his service in a manner of Netzach,
and in a manner of "Netzach Selah va'Ed" that has no cessation
without changes,
and whatever may be and come what may, he stands with strong force,
that even in the land he will be bound with Hashem Echad,
then they give him the treasures from above,
which are also drawn from a place that is above the matter of changes,
"there is no left in this Atika"
and consequently the drawing from there is in a manner of Netzach Selah va'Ed that has no cessation.
And this level they give in a manner of lavish giving without calculations.
And although the giving of the treasures is through the ministers and officers of war,
the Nesi'im of Yisrael in every generation,
down to the Nasi of our generation, the Baal HaHilula,
nevertheless, the main intention in this is that the treasures be drawn down and given to the men of valor,
the hosts of Hashem,
through whom the victory is actually accomplished,
that it will be "and Hashem will be King,"
"and Hashem will be King over all the earth; on that day Hashem will be One and His Name One,"
in the true and complete redemption, speedily, through our righteous Moshiach.
